title: Countable measurable gluing by first index
statement: Let X and Y be measurable spaces, Y having a zero element 0, let S_j ⊆ X (j ∈ ℕ) be measurable sets and G_j : X → Y (j ∈ ℕ) measurable maps. Then there is a measurable L : X → Y with L(x) = 0 for every x ∉ ⋃_j S_j, such that every x ∈ ⋃_j S_j admits j with x ∈ S_j and L(x) = G_j(x).
lean_statement: ∀ (X Y : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Y] [Zero Y] (S : ℕ → Set X) (G : ℕ → X → Y), (∀ j, MeasurableSet (S j)) → (∀ j, Measurable (G j)) → ∃ L : X → Y, Measurable L ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ (⋃ j, S j) → L x = 0) ∧ ∀ x ∈ (⋃ j, S j), ∃ j, x ∈ S j ∧ L x = G j x
